column3: Default core/game baselines support collection/export and are not runtime fallback stores.
Runtime selected-language game store precedes selected-language core store.
Positional lookup uses the supplied integer index; domain number alone does not choose representation.
Text-key lookup normalizes the input key before querying current stores.
Key normalization removes a whitespace run beginning at a line start.
Key normalization next removes a whitespace run ending at a line end.
Remaining whitespace runs of length at least two become one ASCII space.
Key normalization does not normalize the selected translated value.
Species name producer and name getter use a text-key hash rather than a numeric domain-position example.
Move name producer and name getter use a text-key hash rather than a numeric domain-position example.
Event text is registered under its map ID.
Common-event text is registered in event bucket zero.
Under the stated T/U fixture, A plus two LF plus B selects T.
Under the stated T/U fixture, A plus one LF plus B selects T.
Under the stated T/U fixture, A plus two ASCII spaces plus B selects U.
An already selected value containing two LF retains both before window processing.
Input content trimming precedes denormalization; key normalization follows denormalization.
LANGUAGES is declared empty in the fixed configuration.
A configured language entry supplies a display name and a filename fragment.
Boot asks for language only when adapted save data is empty and at least two languages are configured.
The load menu offers language when at least two language entries are configured.
The debug export target chooses author materials and does not itself choose the current player language.
Boot directly loads selected-language files before later lookup.
A Translation constructed with a delayed filename loads it on its first lookup.
The selected language is stored in PokemonSystem rather than the player progress object.
With existing adapted save data, load-menu language choice updates that hash then directly dumps it to the save path.
Without existing adapted save data, load-menu language choice does not write a save file.
Numeric lookup returns a truthy current-game entry before inspecting current-core.
Numeric lookup uses a truthy current-core entry only after current-game misses.
Numeric lookup returns an empty string on a complete miss.
Hash lookup returns the input text when its normalized key is nil or empty.
Hash lookup returns a truthy current-game entry before current-core.
Hash lookup returns a truthy current-core entry after current-game misses.
Hash lookup returns input text after both current stores miss.
Map lookup first checks selected-language game at the requested map ID.
After local game miss, map lookup checks selected-language game bucket zero.
After both game checks miss, map lookup checks selected-language core at requested map ID.
After local core miss, map lookup checks selected-language core bucket zero.
After all four map layers miss, map lookup returns original input text.
Specified UI image identity strings are looked up in SCRIPT_TEXTS.
Specified image identity lookup occurs before image creation/loading.
A selected nonempty image-identity translation is handed to the resource consumer even if the original resource exists.
Control help translates seven key image identities.
Control-help background identity is independent of those seven translated keys.
Graphical battle menus translate listed cursor/type/Mega/shift identities.
The corresponding battle menu backgrounds are independent resource identities.
Trainer card image identities use translation, including the female variant behind its additional resource-existence gate.
Trainer-card background and badges have separate fixed resource identities.
Voltorb Flip translates background and memo basenames then retains that consumer's directory prefix.
Other Voltorb Flip tile/cursor resources are separate fixed identities.
An empty image-identity translation remains a hit; resource resolution decides the later effect.
The localization lookup provides no generic retry of the original image after translated-resource failure.
A later resource failure does not imply previously created viewport/images were rolled back.
A truthy empty string is returned directly instead of selecting a lower language layer.
Ordinary selected-language loading failure clears both current stores.
Selected-language loading validates the outer Array only.
Malformed inner containers can raise during lookup without being rescued by that lookup method.
Script formatters rescue only translation lookup and use the source argument on that exception.
Errors in clone/substitution/formatting occur outside that script lookup rescue.
Map formatters do not provide the script lookup rescue.
Hash lookup returns the stored value object without cloning it for each caller.
The map-name consumer expands uppercase player-name control text in the selected material.
An empty language lookup can reach a separate map-name base-name fallback without changing localization precedence.
Plain replacement iterates provided arguments in order.
Formatted replacement evaluates the placeholder format with sprintf.
A missing parameter leaves its corresponding placeholder untouched.
The plain script fixture X{1}Y with Q returns XQY before a window.
The plain script fixture with backslash-and-ampersand replacement restores the matched placeholder.
The plain script fixture with backslash-and-digit-one replacement returns XY.
The map plain fixture with backslash-and-ampersand replacement restores its placeholder.
The map plain fixture with backslash-and-digit-one replacement returns XY.
The script formatted string fixture retains the literal backslash-and-ampersand parameter.
The map formatted string fixture retains the literal backslash-and-ampersand parameter.
Historical isolated Ruby receipts support only their named fixtures, not current host/window execution.
Collection scans each already loaded script archive section.
Only archive section count one enables the additional Data/Scripts traversal.
The additional traversal scans every returned file rather than filtering by .rb here.
An existing plugin archive is loaded and its compressed script strings are scanned after ordinary scripts.
The script scanner accepts the initial double-quoted literal fragment after _INTL or _ISPRINTF.
The event-script scanner accepts the corresponding double-quoted fragment after _I.
Single-quoted input is not recognized by those literal scanners.
A matching literal in a comment can be collected without proving runtime reachability.
Ordinary-script decoding performs CR, LF, control-one, escaped-quote and double-backslash transformations in that order.
Event-script decoding transforms escaped quotes then double backslashes without decoding literal backslash-n to LF.
A continued display-text line adds one space after nonempty accumulated text.
A noncontinuation-triggered commit normalizes the specified post-nonpunctuation whitespace run.
The final pending-text commit at list end skips that additional normalization.
Collected script candidates append to SCRIPT_TEXTS hash material.
Collected common-event candidates replace event-map bucket zero.
A map event bucket is replaced only when its collected candidate list is nonempty.
Collection catches Hangup and can return after installing only a prefix of buckets.
Other collection exceptions propagate along the actual caller path.
Compiler invokes collection after earlier compilation and saves default messages afterwards.
The stated double-backslash-n source spelling can yield a collected key different from its runtime input key.
A translation present only under that collected key does not make the distinct runtime key hit.
Later window newline processing cannot prove the earlier localization lookup hit.
Successful receive-item pocket-message lookup happens after its inventory addition.
Successful item-ball pocket-message lookup happens after its inventory addition.
Successful prize pocket-message lookup happens after its inventory addition.
Successful berry harvest pocket-message lookup happens after its inventory addition.
A normal lookup miss returns fallback and does not undo those earlier inventory writes.
Default hash collection excludes incoming keys already in default-core at the same domain/map.
The default-core filter compares keys rather than candidate text values.
Replacement collection starts with a new game-domain container.
Append collection retains its prior game-domain container.
A candidate rejected by the core-key filter does not delete an old game key retained by append.
Map-m collection filters against default-core map-m rather than borrowing shared map zero.
A nil hash candidate is skipped.
An empty-string hash candidate can be stored before export later skips empty source values.
The stated core-A/game-Z replacement fixture leaves only B.
The stated core-A/game-Z append fixture retains Z and adds B.
The append fixture retains old game A and Z even though incoming A is core-filtered.
The corresponding replacement fixture leaves only B.
Ordinary move-name and move-description validation use replacement collection.
Form-name/text validation uses append collection.
Script gathering uses append collection.
Cancelling the debug core/game choice after target-language selection returns before invoking extraction.
Successful author export does not itself write player language or switch current message stores.
Export uses Text_<language>_core or Text_<language>_game folders.
Array export writes index, original and translation as three lines.
Hash export writes key and translation as two lines.
An occupied export destination asks before replacing its files.
Refusal returns before deleting or writing destination files.
Accepted replacement deletes every file returned by recursive destination traversal, without limiting to .txt.
Replacement preserves destination and nested directory objects.
An empty selected baseline is reported and returns before destination mutation.
A later export I/O error can preserve a partial deletion/write prefix without restoration.
Actual CR/LF/TAB/control-one triggers export encoding.
A bracket at a line start triggers encoding; a sole preceding ASCII space does not.
Once triggered, encoding transforms all listed controls and all brackets in the value.
Import recognizes sections before reversing export encodings.
Only nonempty baseline source entries drive exported records.
A target-language-only key absent from baseline does not create an extra exported record.
Export can iterate domain IDs beyond baseline length when language material is longer.
That outer iteration does not guarantee absent/malformed event-domain containers are safe.
A bare [Q] translation is encoded and can round-trip in the stated single hash record.
A space-prefixed [Q] without control characters becomes a section header and first causes the prior one-line hash section to fail.
Adding a real TAB triggers bracket encoding and avoids that same premature header case.
Merged event export stops its presence precheck at the first nil map bucket.
An existing empty map bucket does not stop that precheck.
No nonempty bucket before that nil causes the entire merged event file to be skipped.
Once the precheck finds text, actual merged writing skips empty/nil buckets and can include later buckets.
Separate-map export can skip absent/empty buckets and continue to a later valid map, given MapInfos.
Accepted destination deletion occurs before the sparse merged-file decision.
Compilation discovers .txt inputs under its selected Text_<fragment> directory.
Section preprocessing skips raw whitespace-only lines.
Section preprocessing skips raw lines whose first column is #.
A preceding ASCII space prevents that raw comment test, after which content trimming can expose # as data.
A content-internal # is retained rather than PBS-style suffix stripping.
Retained content lines are stripped at their ends before interpretation.
A section with no retained content is skipped.
Section-name validation happens before representation and line-count interpretation.
A nonzero to_i prefix selects its integer ID without demanding an all-numeric section name.
After to_i zero, a recognized MessageTypes constant supplies the section ID.
After prior name branches miss, a case-insensitive Map plus digits selects an event-map ID.
Numeric section name 0 is rejected while EVENT_TEXTS can identify domain zero.
A final negative section ID is rejected.
A section's first retained content line chooses array versus hash independently of its domain ID.
A Map section classified as array is rejected before its three-line divisibility check.
An array section requires content count divisible by three.
A hash section requires even content count.
Each later array record independently requires a numeric index line.
A two-line SCRIPT_TEXTS hash export beginning with 123 is reclassified as array and rejected by record width.
Array index zero can be accepted independently of numeric section-name zero rejection.
Complete compilation opens output in wb before input directory discovery/parsing.
Ensure closes a failed complete compilation output without restoring its prior contents.
The menu's selected Text_*_* fragment includes core/game and determines the messages_<fragment>.dat output.
A single exported empty translation loses its empty line during preprocessing and fails odd hash width.
A column-zero #Word translation is dropped as comment and causes the same odd-width failure.
A space-prefixed #Word survives the raw comment test, trims, and is imported as the translated value.
Unprotected ordinary end spaces are trimmed from a value during import.
Encoded TAB markers survive preprocessing and decode back to end TABs.
Calling only the single-file parser does not open or truncate an output artifact.
Within a hash section, a later value for the same normalized key overwrites the earlier value.
Distinct raw keys colliding after normalization use the later value.
Within an array section, a later value at the same index overwrites the earlier value.
A later same-shape section merges its supplied keys into the accumulated domain.
That merge preserves prior unique keys not supplied by the later section.
A later sparse array section preserves prior populated indices omitted by the later section.
Complete compilation feeds sorted input files into the same accumulated collection.
The stated array-then-hash nonnumeric-key fixture fails with TypeError under the cited Ruby semantics.
A failure while merging the later mixed section leaves the already accumulated prior section in memory.
The one mixed-shape failure does not establish all mixed inputs fail or all same-shape rules apply to them.
